title: ACID and the CAP theorem: what you gain and what you give up

videos.script: A library lends its last copy of a book twice. {{twice}} Nobody wrote a line you could point at. Two desks read the same number, and both believed it. {{desks}} This lesson is about the guarantees that stop that, and about what each one costs. First, ACID. A transaction that fails halfway leaves nothing behind. You will watch a reservation vanish without one, and survive with one. {{acid}} Then isolation. Two connections to one SQLite file play two desks at once, and lose an update. {{isolation}} Then the unit of work, the pattern that gives business code one transaction without any SQL in it. {{uow}} After that, the library opens a second branch, and the link between the two can fail. {{branches}} CAP says what you must decide for that day. PACELC says what you are deciding on every other day, when nothing is broken and the only enemy is distance. {{pacelc}} And the answer is not one choice for the whole system. Lending the last copy wants one answer. Showing the shelf on a web page wants another. {{choosing}}
